newsitem.title: CHINA: Malaysia minister encouraged by China palm quota.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia minister encouraged by China palm quota.

text.p: Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik said on Monday he was encouraged by China's palm oil import quota of 1.3 million tonnes between now and next March.
"It has been approved and will be distributed to the provinces and refiners," he told reporters.

Malaysian palm oil prices surged on Friday on confirmation of market talk of the quota. The benchmark third position November crude palm oil futures rose 36 ringgit ($14.4) to 1,196 ringgit a tonne in Friday trade.
Prices were up another eight ringgit at 1,204 ringgit per tonne at midday on Monday.
Traders and refiners said, however, they doubted the quota would translate into real deals as high prices were deterring Chinese importers who have been buying cheaper soybean oil.
Lim, who is in Beijing with a Malaysian trade delegation, said China would eventually buy palm oil and this would mean business for Malaysia.
He said previously that he believed 80 percent of the imports would come from Malaysia.
